**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

- **Governing law (§ 18.3, p0765):** New York law, conflict-of-laws excluded, CISG excluded — exactly the playbook's *preferred* position.
- **Forum (§ 17.3, p0747–p0748):** mandatory ICC arbitration rather than New York courts, but the seat is Osaka when Array demands and New York when Ono demands. As the Japanese party, we either arbitrate at home or in an accepted venue; there is no exclusive foreign seat in the counterparty's home jurisdiction, so the walk-away trigger ("mandatory arbitration seated abroad" / vendor's home venue) is not engaged.
- **Additional support:** § 17.3(g) preserves each Party's right to seek provisional and conservatory relief in any court of competent jurisdiction.

The arbitration-instead-of-courts mechanic is a sub-element short of the preferred wording that runs in our favour, so it is noted in the rationale rather than flagged.
